headline: Curated genome-scale metabolic models extended for fermentation and ME-model analysis
label: Genome Scale Metabolic Modeling
summary: Recent preprints extend curated metabolic reconstructions and ME-models to fermentation data, RNA decay and NADH-regulated acetate flux.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the construction and extension of metabolic models that are constrained by explicit data or mechanistic detail. iJL1143 is a curated genome-scale reconstruction of the mycoprotein fungus Fusarium venenatum A3/5, built from an A. niger template and validated against batch fermentation biomass data. coralME v1.3 extends ME-model analysis to non-canonical amino acid translation, protein and RNA degradation reactions, arbitrary coupling coefficients, and cofactor essentiality in bacterial models. The E. coli study is a kinetic model rather than a genome-scale reconstruction. It covers pyruvate metabolism, the TCA cycle and acetate formation, includes NADH inhibition of pyruvate dehydrogenase and citrate synthase, and is Bayesian-calibrated to test NADH regulation of competing acetate flux responses. What is new across these items is the expansion of model scope: to a non-model fungal production organism, to proteome and RNA turnover processes, and to regulatory kinetics linking cofactor state to flux.
